newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF not yet considered measures against DKB.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF not yet considered measures against DKB.

text.p: The Ministry of Finance (MOF) said on Wednesday it has not yet started considering measures it might take against Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB), a major underwriter of Japanese government bonds (JGB).
A MOF official told Reuters: "We have not yet started considering what to do about DKB."
A scandal involving Nomura Securities Co Ltd widened on Tuesday when prosecutors raided DKB's headquarters and the homes of several of the bank's officials.

A spokesman for DKB said on Tuesday the bank would cooperate with the investigation, which Deputy Chief Prosecutor Kunihiro Matsuo said was linked to the probe into the Nomura payoff and racketeer scandal.

On May 13, MOF announced the suspension of Nomura from JGB auctions and bond underwriting until the implementation of administrative punishments against the brokerage proposed by the Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC).
Meanwhile, an official at the Ministry of Home Affairs, which oversees municipal governments and their bond issues, said on Wednesday it would wait and see the progress of the investigation.
"Nothing has been decided yet," the official said.

Prosecutors last week arrested racketeer Ryuichi Koike and raided Nomura's head office and branches after taking in two former Nomura managing directors and another senior official suspected of violating Japan's Commercial Code and Securities and Exchange Law with payoffs to the "sokaiya" racketeer.
The Commercial Code bans companies from making payments to "sokaiya", racketeers who typically extort money from companies by threatening to disrupt shareholder meetings.
